related_questions.question: What are the new rules for traveling?

text_blocks.snippet: Several new travel rules are taking effect in 2025. Most notably, the REAL ID Act will require a REAL ID-compliant driver's license or other TSA-approved ID for domestic air travel starting May 7, 2025. Additionally, the UK will require a Electronic Travel Authorization (ETA) for US citizens beginning January 8, 2025. Finally, the EU's Entry/Exit System (EES) is expected to become operational in October 2025, impacting how non-EU nationals enter the Schengen Area.
snippet_highlighted_words: the REAL ID Act will require a REAL ID-compliant driver's license or other TSA-approved ID for domestic air travel starting May 7, 2025

list.snippet: Starting May 7, 2025, you will need a REAL ID-compliant driver's license or other acceptable form of identification (like a passport or passport card) to board domestic flights and access certain federal facilities.
You can check if your current state-issued ID is REAL ID compliant by visiting your state's DMV website.
Acceptable forms of ID include: REAL ID-compliant driver's licenses or state-issued photo IDs, enhanced driver's licenses, U.S. passports, U.S. passport cards, and certain DHS trusted traveler cards.
U.S. citizens traveling to the UK will need to apply for an ETA before their trip, starting January 8, 2025.
The ETA is an electronic travel authorization that will cost around $13 and be valid for multiple trips over two years or until your passport expires.
You can apply for the ETA on the official UK ETA website.
The EES will register all non-EU nationals entering the Schengen Area, replacing the manual stamping of passports with electronic recordings.
It will collect passport details and biometric information (fingerprints and facial image).
The EES is expected to become operational in October 2025 and will be phased in over six months.
This system will apply to U.S. citizens traveling to the Schengen Area.
